subject: Indemnity playbook — evidence retention, model-output sandboxing, and cost-share for third-party IP claims
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Anya Petrova <anya@brightfarm.com>
Cc: Jordan Harrison <jharrison@harrisonlaw.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Indemnity playbook — initial evidence + cost-share thinking

Hi all,

Following up from last week's contract call with BrightFarm — they pushed back on two things that are converging: (1) what evidence we need if they claim third-party IP infringement tied to model outputs, and (2) whether there's a proportional cost-share if litigation/defense costs exceed X.

To move quickly, I attached an "evidence_checklist_v1.pdf" that maps the kinds of artifacts Legal/CS will need (logs, prompt/response captures, model version + quantization metadata, deployment region, customer-supplied assets).

Key asks:
- Kimberly: can Legal confirm which items we must insist on in the MSA vs. which can live in an Order Form / playbook?
- Ben: commercial — BrightFarm wants a cap/offset for defense costs if the claim arises from customer data they supplied. Can you draft short phrasing that gives them comfort but preserves our defend/control stance?
- Marissa: CS / Solutions — confirm whether we can reasonably collect the evidence items without customer-facing SDK changes (ideally server-side retention).

Goal: have a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a proposed redline to the Order Form by EOD Thu.

Thanks,

Tessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_checklist_v1.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Anya Petrova <anya@brightfarm.com>
Cc: Jordan Harrison <jharrison@harrisonlaw.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity playbook — initial evidence + cost-share thinking

Tessa — thanks and good summary. Quick Legal take:

- MSA vs Order Form: core allocation (defend/control, indemnity trigger) should stay in the MSA. Operational details (evidence submission SLA, retention windows, sandboxing requirements) can be in an Order Form appendix or a Playbook that we reference in the MSA. That keeps the contract short and lets us iterate operationally.

- Evidence list: the attached checklist is good. A couple of edits before we ask them to accept:
  * Add a row clarifying we need the exact model hash and runtime environment (cuda/cuDNN versions) for forensic reproduction.
  * Narrow retention requests to "last 90 days of request/response traces" unless customer opts into longer retention.

- Defend/control: we should keep defend/control for third-party IP claims but add a narrow exception where Customer-supplied code or data is the sole proximate cause (i.e., we didn't modify it). For those, we can propose a cost-share.

I've attached a one-page "msa_redline_cheatsheet.xlsx" that maps proposed language locations. I'll draft redline language for the Order Form appendix that lists the evidence SLA and the required metadata fields.

K
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: msa_redline_cheatsheet.xlsx

Short commercial note — BrightFarm wants an express cost-sharing bucket if litigation exceeds $250k and it's not clearly our model design bug. My proposal (high level) we discussed on the call:

- If claim arises solely from Customer-supplied assets or configuration, we default to 50/50 defense cost-split up to a $500k shared cap, after which each party bears their own incremental costs.
- If claim arises from model-generated output with no Customer-supplied content, Redwood defends.

This is a compromise that buys them comfort while protecting our defend/control posture. I'll work with Pricing to model unit economics impact and follow up with a short clause that Legal can evaluate.

-Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-21T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity playbook — initial evidence + cost-share thinking

Tessa/Kimberly/Ben — thanks for the context. From an external counsel perspective:

- Drafting note: we can keep defend/control but add a narrowly tailored "contributory cause" carve that permits cost-sharing tied to a defined discovery showing Customer contribution to the infringement risk. Suggested mechanics:
  * A 30-day forensic window where Customer must provide the listed artifacts (logs + original assets). Failure to produce within 30 days shifts rebuttable presumption that Customer contributed.
  * Cost-sharing banding tied to causation tiers (e.g., 25%/50%/75% depending on evidence showing extent of customer contribution).

- Evidence preservation: propose a "technical sandbox" definition in the Order Form Appendix that describes how we snapshot prompt/context and model version. That avoids asking the MSA to include technical minutiae.

- Discovery and privileges: recommend we add language protecting Redwood's internal security telemetry (we can provide summaries and hashes but resist handing raw KV caches unless ordered by court).

I'll send a redline to the Order Form appendix and a short memo with the proposed banding. Expect that by EOD Wed.

Jordan Harrison
Harrison & Co. LLP
External Counsel to BrightFarm

Thanks everyone — helpful alignment. Quick summary / mutual action plan (MAP):

1) Legal (Kimberly + Jordan): exchange an Order Form appendix redline that
   - lists the evidence SLA (30-day production for primary artifacts),
   - defines the technical sandbox snapshot (model hash, runtime metadata, truncated traces), and
   - includes a privilege-preserving approach for telemetry hashes only.
   Deliverable: redline + 1-page memo by COB Wed (Kimberly/Jordan).

2) Commercial (Ben): provide proposed cost-sharing clause language and a short note on the commercial cap (Ben to run $ impact). Deliverable: draft clause by Tue EOD.

3) Solutions/CS (Marissa): confirm feasibility of retaining traces server-side for 90 days and whether we need an SDK opt-in. Deliverable: ops feasibility email + any implementation risks by Tue EOD.

4) Tessa: I'll consolidate and send a single redline to BrightFarm next Thu with a short executive cover note.

Attachments included for internal reference: evidence_checklist_v1.pdf, msa_redline_cheatsheet.xlsx, proposed-cost-share-term.docx

If no objections, I'll mark this MAP in HubSpot and book a 30-min alignment call Thurs 9am PT.

Tessa Morgan
